title: Your seeking is from Him
hook: the fact that you seek Him is already His gift
tomorrow: a door opens and you feel underqualified. walk in?

segments.voice: Yesterday: delay isn't refusal. The asking is heard; the answer comes in His choice and His time. Delayed, not denied. Today, the asking's source.
screen: `DELAYED, NOT DENIED.` → `WHERE DOES ASKING COME FROM?`

segments.voice: A playlist that knows your mood before you do. An ad for the shoes you mentioned once, out loud, near your phone. Some days it feels like every want you have was planted by something. Ibn Ata'illah, long before any feed, asked the same question about the best want of all: the wish to come close to God. Who put the wanting in you in the first place? You, or Him? Inside Islam there are two honest ways to lean, and today both get to speak.
screen: `A PLAYLIST THAT KNOWS YOU.` → `WHO PLANTED THE WANT?` → `TWO WAYS TO LEAN.`

segments.voice: The first voice leans on effort. The Qur'an says that those who strive for God's sake, He will guide to His paths. Al-Bukhari keeps a hadith qudsi, God's words told by the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him: whoever comes near to Me by a hand's span, I come near by an arm's length; whoever comes walking, I come running. The person moves first, and God answers bigger. Its best point: it keeps you responsible. Nobody wakes up for fajr on your behalf. The second voice leans on gift. Ibn Ata'illah, paraphrased: the fact that you're seeking Him is already His gift to you. You wouldn't want Him unless He had put the wanting there. This side has its own verse: you will not will, unless God wills. Its best point: it guards against pride. Your prayer streak isn't a trophy, because even the first step was handed to you. Notice that neither voice tells you to do less. The effort voice doesn't say grace is unreal, and Ibn Ata'illah never says skip the alarm. Plenty of room, then, to hold both at once: strive with everything, and thank Him for the striving. The real difference is what comes first in the heart when you notice you want to pray. One voice says, I showed up. The other says, I was invited. The wanting is His gift.
screen: `ONE: STRIVE, AND HE GUIDES.` · `A HAND'S SPAN, AN ARM'S LENGTH.` · `TWO: THE SEEKING IS HIS GIFT.` · `OR HOLD BOTH AT ONCE.` · then, large: `THE WANTING IS HIS GIFT.`

segments.voice: On your fingers, count three moments when you wanted something good: to be kinder, to pray, to forgive someone, to start over. It doesn't matter whether you followed through. For each one, give a quiet thank you, to God if you pray, or simply to the wanting itself for showing up.
Your seeking is from Him: Ibn Ata'illah's reminder that the wish to come close is already a gift, not a trophy.
screen: `YOUR SEEKING IS FROM HIM — today's word`.

segments.voice: For the alarm tomorrow morning: the wanting is His gift, and so is the alarm you set for it. Five sayings down.

screen: `DAY 1627 COUNTS.` → `IBN ATA'ILLAH · 5 OF 6.` → `TOMORROW: A DOOR OPENS. YOU FEEL UNDERQUALIFIED.`

howItsDone: In Muslim teaching, striving in worship goes together with thanking God for the ability to strive; saying alhamdulillah after a prayer treats the prayer itself as a gift.

fork.setup: you lean toward the effort side. a friend says, 'it's all gift; my effort is nothing.' state her side at its best.
options: it keeps her from treating her prayer like a trophy to show off.
it means she can skip prayer until she feels the gift arrive.
it proves effort is pointless, so nobody needs to try at all.
fork.reveal: the gift voice guards against pride: even the first step was handed to you. it never excuses skipping the steps.

original.note: Arabic: seeking, searching; the seeking Ibn Ata'illah calls His gift.

trapdoor: what you thought: either you earn closeness, or God hands it out. pick one.
what it means: strive fully, and see even the wish to strive as given.
what a scholar hears: old questions about human acts and God's will sit underneath; Ibn Ata'illah answers them as a teacher of the heart, not as a debater.
guess: the wish to find God is itself God's gift
you must earn God before you may seek Him
seeking God means leaving ordinary life

chat.says: praying fajr on time since the deferral. dadi says 'that's not you, that's a gift.' i set the alarms tho??
options: Both are true. You set the alarms, and the wanting to set them was His gift.
She's right, so the alarms don't matter; if it's a gift, effort adds nothing.
You're right; it's your discipline, and calling it a gift is just modesty.
chat.meaning: Both can be held: strive with everything, and thank Him for the striving. Ibn Ata'illah: the seeking itself is His gift.

hadith qudsi.meaning: words of God told by the Prophet, outside the Qur'an

Ibn Ata'illah.meaning: a Sufi teacher in Egypt who wrote al-Hikam

al-Bukhari.meaning: a classical hadith scholar; his Sahih is a major collection

sources.ref: Ibn Ata'illah al-Iskandari, al-Hikam (the aphorism that your seeking Him is from Him)
Qur'an 29:69 (those who strive for Us, We will guide in Our ways)

Qur'an 76:30 (you will not will unless God wills)
